subject: Headless verifier started after hand-in copies the ticket branch head; apply.sh records every OBJECTION line of worker and verifier EVIDENCE
objective: Written against the shape #155 lands (no --prepare, verifier_copy inlined into start_verifier_bg). (1) start_verifier_bg picks the copy source the way #149's --prepare verifier did: interface_fixed true -> ticket base_sha (unchanged, parallel with the worker); otherwise, branch t<n> with >= 1 commit over base_sha -> archive of the branch head, and the verifier dispatch packet gets a 'copy source' paragraph naming the branch and head sha and saying verify-case.py red --ref stays the ticket base_sha; otherwise (0 commits) the verifier is not started and stderr says so. archive_copy stays called exactly once, inside start_verifier_bg. (2) apply.sh feeds every ^OBJECTION: line of the --evidence file AND of each --evidence-verifier file to ticket.py objection (with that file as --evidence), not only grep -m1 of --evidence; any line that comes back fresh (rc 0) or undisposed (rc 3) makes apply exit 6 after all lines are recorded; ticket.py objection rc 2 on any line keeps today's rc-2 path. ticket.py record_objection (category + body match) is unchanged. (3) Parallel verifier receipt: when patch-verify does not apply to the branch head (git apply --check fails), apply.sh tries a per-file 3-way merge instead of exiting 3 at once: ancestor = the tree the verifier copy was made from (new optional flag --verifier-base <sha>, passed by auto-fix with the sha start_verifier_bg archived; absent -> ticket base_sha; must be an ancestor of the branch head, else rc 2), ours = branch head, theirs = ancestor + patch-verify (git merge-file --diff3 semantics). Clean merges are staged. A conflict whose ancestor section is empty (both sides inserted at the same spot, e.g. both appended classes at EOF) is resolved ours-then-theirs ONLY for *.py files, and the result must ast-parse and must not define the same module-level name twice; otherwise, or any conflict with a non-empty ancestor section, or any conflict in a non-.py file -> rc 3 as today, branch head and worktree untouched, stderr names each file and the conflicting line range or duplicated name. After staging, the existing hard_block check and the single patch-verify commit run unchanged; the commit message gains one line '3-way: <file>, ...' listing merged files. (4) The verifier dispatch packet in the parallel mode (interface_fixed true) gains one paragraph: new cases go in new classes appended at the end of the existing module, helpers live inside the verifier's class, no new module-level names (D-056 1: no new ticket-numbered case files).
